One content item: its code, its written arguments, its own part

Source: R/item_ops.R
tfl_item_code.Rd

  • tfl_item_code(): the item's one call, as tfl_content_code() writes it (no plan <-, no pipe).

  • tfl_item_written(): the names of the arguments its code writes – the arguments given, an !unset or NULL one left out; a verb's positional ... (plan_titles("A", "B")) is "...".

  • tfl_item_own(): what the report's own layer holds of the item, given the item below it (the layers' without the report's own, tfl_resolve_output()'s provenance = TRUE). A verb whose ... is named (plan_cells() ...) keeps only the keys whose value differs from below's, and a key below has that the item has not is !unset; any other verb is the item whole, or NULL when it is the same as below's (the own item can go). Values are compared as their R text, so 30 and 30L are the same.

Usage

tfl_item_code(item, pipe = NULL)

tfl_item_written(item)

tfl_item_own(item, below = NULL)

Arguments

item

A tfl_item().

pipe

Unused: the call alone (kept for the code's form to come).

below

The item below it, or NULL (no layer has the verb: the item is all the report's own).

Value

tfl_item_code(): the code, one element a line. tfl_item_written(): the argument names. tfl_item_own(): a tfl_item() or NULL.

Examples

it <- tfl_item("plan_cells", list(continuous = list(n = "{N}"), default = "{n} ({p}%)"))
tfl_item_code(it)
#> [1] "plan_cells(continuous = list(n = \"{N}\"), default = \"{n} ({p}%)\")"
tfl_item_written(it)
#> [1] "continuous" "default"   
below <- tfl_item("plan_cells", list(default = "{n} ({p}%)"), from = "defaults")
tfl_item_own(it, below)$args
#> $continuous
#> $continuous$n
#> [1] "{N}"
#> 
#>
